Image 32: Buy Me a Coffee logo [...] We are a small family shop. We made our first sales on Oct 17 — $8 total. To receive a first payout, Buy Me a Coffee requires a review on its payout settings page, but that page renders blank below the Stripe card — for us in multiple browsers and for the owner on his own phone. We emailed support on Oct 15 (no answer), then twice on Oct 21 with our review answers and screenshots. Support finally replied Oct 22 saying our details went to their moderation team and the funds 'should be paid out by October 24.' By then we had already decided to close: a week of silence and a payout page that never worked is not a foundation a family can build on. The shop tools themselves were fine; getting paid and getting an answer were not.

Review Buy Me a Coffee?

Reviewers see Buy Me a Coffee as easy to use for tips, memberships, digital products, and direct messages, and some say the familiar brand helps supporters trust it. Longtime users describe it as simple and useful for small creator communities. But the sharpest, most repeated criticism is payouts: many users report delayed or blocked withdrawals, account suspensions or re-verification issues, refund problems, and slow or inconsistent support. Overall, people like the concept and basic tools, but trust drops when money or account access is on the line.

Terrible experience with Buy Me a Coffee. If you’re thinking of bringing your donors to this platform, consider this a warning. I had my Chase account connected with all the required verification details, yet there was nobody to actually talk to.
